status: Mistrial declared Sept. 4, 2026 after a deadlocked jury. The Plymouth County District Attorney has not announced whether Lindsay Clancy will be retried.

hearings.title: District court arraignment
hearings.note: Clancy appeared by video from Tewksbury State Hospital, pleaded not guilty and was held without bail.

hearings.title: Superior Court arraignment
hearings.note: Held at the hospital rather than in a courtroom, after the Sept. 15, 2023 grand jury indictments.

hearings.title: Bifurcation ruling
hearings.note: The defense asked to split the trial so the jury decides the facts before criminal responsibility. The court denied it. The filings are not public.

hearings.title: Dispute over New Yorker interview recordings
hearings.note: Prosecutors sought recordings of the magazine's interviews with Patrick Clancy. The magazine resisted on First Amendment grounds and the dispute delayed the trial. The filings are not public.

hearings.title: Dispute over psychiatric records
hearings.note: Prosecutors sought Clancy's medical records. Argued together with the reporter's notes question. The filings are not public.

hearings.title: Request by the father of the child victims
hearings.note: A July 24 order granted part of it. The order is described by the source site but not posted.

hearings.title: Mistrial and emergency petition
hearings.note: The judge declared a mistrial. The Supreme Judicial Court denied the defense's emergency stay request.

updates.t: Judge declares a mistrial after the jury reports it cannot reach a unanimous decision. Clancy is expected to remain in a state psychiatric hospital. The DA says a retrial decision is coming.

Judge impounds the 911 call and autopsy photographs at the request of the father; media may not record or display them. Both could still be presented to the jury and seen by the public in the courtroom.
